stem: Supreme Court's judgment of Indra Sawhney vs Union of India Case is related to which issue?

options.label: a
options.text: Regarding the issue of OBC reservation in Government employment

options.label: c
options.text: Approve the reservation on promotion of SC

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: In Indra Sawhney vs. Union of India (1992), the decision of the 9-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court is related to reservation for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in government jobs. In this landmark judgment, the Supreme Court upheld the government’s decision to provide 27% reservation to OBCs on the basis of the Mandal Commission report; however, it also held that the “creamy layer” or the economically advanced section among OBCs should be kept outside its scope. Further, the Supreme Court also laid down that the total reservation provided under Articles 15(4) and 16(4) should not exceed the limit of 50%.

stem: The mobile court in India is the brain child of –
expl: The concept of mobile courts in India was first envisioned by Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam. Therefore, mobile courts are regarded as his “brainchild”. On 4 August 2007, the country’s first mobile court was inaugurated in Punhana, located in the present Nuh district of Haryana (then Mewat district). It was inaugurated by the then Chief Justice of India, K.G. Balakrishnan. Its objective is to extend the benefits of the judicial system to remote and backward areas.

stem: In which state was the first “lokayukta” established?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Maharashtra was the first state in India where the Lokayukta office was established in 1972 under the “Maharashtra Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act, 1971”. Odisha was the first state to pass legislation related to the establishment of Lokayukta (in 1970), but the institution came into existence there only in 1983.

stem: In Indian administration, the “Split System” is related to—

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: In the Indian administrative system, the Split System is related to policy-making and its implementation. In this system, the Secretariat performs planning and policy-making functions, while the implementation of policies is carried out by the concerned Directorate.

stem: Function of Bureaucracy—
expl: The main function of bureaucracy is the running of administration. After the legislature makes rules/laws, it assigns the executive the responsibility to implement those rules/laws. The executive gets these rules/laws implemented through the bureaucracy. Along with this, the bureaucracy also assists ministers in day-to-day functioning.

stem: Who decides the disqualification of members of State legislative Assembly, for matters other than those in the tenth schedule of the Constitution?
expl: According to Article 192 of the Constitution, the Governor decides the question of disqualification (except matters related to the Tenth Schedule) of a member of a State Legislature. However, in this matter, the Governor acts according to the opinion of the Election Commission. But if the question of disqualification arises under the Tenth Schedule (on the ground of defection), then in the case of the Legislative Assembly, the Speaker, and in the case of the Legislative Council, the Chairman gives the decision.

stem: Indian national Flag was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on which date ?
expl: In its fourth session, the Constituent Assembly adopted the Indian National Flag on 22 July, 1947. The chakra in the middle of the National Flag has 24 spokes, and the ratio of the flag’s length to breadth is 3:2.

stem: Which one of the following characteristics is not true for unitary form of Government?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above /More than one of the above

expl: In a unitary (central) system, supreme power is divided between the central authority and its different subordinate units. Generally, in a federal system there are two levels of governments—one the central government and the other the state government. Different levels of government govern the same group of citizens; but each has its own jurisdiction in law-making, taxation, and administration. Therefore, quick decision-making, flexibility, and uniformity of laws are features of a unitary (central) system; however, it is considered an ideal system for small countries, not for large countries.

stem:
With reference to United nations peacekeeping operations, consider the following statements:
1. United nations peacekeeping forces can only use force for self-defense.
2. A peacekeeping operation can only be withdrawn by a resolution of the United nations Security Council.
3. The United States is the largest budget contributor to Un peacekeeping operations.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Statement 1 is false because the United Nations Peacekeepers can use force for self-defense as well as for the'Defense of the Mandate' given to them. The remaining statements 2 and 3 are true. The United Nations peacekeeping operation can only be started by a resolution adopted by the United Nations Security Council. The United Nations peacekeeping operation is deployed based on the mandate given under this resolution. Also, the duration of the peacekeeping operation can be extended or withdrawn by a resolution of the Security Council. In addition, the United States of America is the largest budget contributor to United Nations peace operations. The United States of America contributed the highest, approximately 26.95 percent, to United Nations peace operations in the year 2024-25.

stem: The headquarters of International Court of Justice is situated at:
expl: The International Court of Justice is located in The Hague, Netherlands (Holland). It was established in 1945 under the United Nations Charter, and it began functioning from April 1946. The International Court of Justice is the only one among the six principal organs of the United Nations that is located outside New York.

stem: Who is the Secretary-General of the United nations?

The Secretary-General is the spokesperson and the chief administrative officer of the United Nations. Kofi Annan, a citizen of the African country Ghana, served as the Secretary-General of the United Nations from 1 January 1997 to 31 December 2006. At present, António Guterres is the Secretary-General of the United Nations.

stem:
Which of the following are matters on which a constitutional amendment is possible only with the ratification of the legislature of not less than one-half of the states?
1. Election of the President.
2. Representation of States in Parliament.
3. Any of the lists in the 7th Schedule.
4. Abolition of the legislative Council of a State.
Choose the correct answer.
expl: The Indian Constitution is flexible and dynamic. As required, it can be amended according to the procedure given in Article 368 of the Constitution. In the Indian Constitution, amendments can be made in three ways— 1. By simple majority—There are some provisions in the Constitution which Parliament can amend by a simple majority. Such amendments are not treated as “amendments of the Constitution” for the purposes of Article 368. For example—changing the names and boundaries of states or creating new states; creating or abolishing Legislative Councils in states; increasing the salaries of the President, Governors, and the judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts, etc. These are done by simple majority. 2. By special majority—Under the procedure of Article 368(2), Parliament can amend most Articles of the Constitution by passing a bill in each House by a special majority (i.e., a majority of the total membership of the House and a two-thirds majority of the members present and voting). 3. By special majority and with state ratification— According to the proviso to Article 368(2), there are certain provisions of the Constitution which require, along with Parliament’s special majority, approval by the legislatures of at least half of the states. For example—election of the President and its procedure; extent of the executive power of the Union and the states; provisions relating to the Supreme Court and High Courts; representation of states in Parliament; Parliament’s power and procedure to amend the Constitution; division of legislative powers between the Union and the states and entries in the lists of the Seventh Schedule; provisions relating to the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council (Article 279A), etc.

stem: Amnesty International is an organization associated with
expl: Amnesty International is a worldwide voluntary organization that works for human rights. It was founded in 1961 by a London barrister, Peter Benenson. In 1961, Peter Benenson wrote an article titled “The Forgotten Prisoners” protesting unethical arrests occurring around the world. Amnesty International is a concrete expression of his ideas. Its headquarters are in London.

options.text: The Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The Chairman of the State Public Service Commission is appointed by the Governor of the State. However, the President has the power to remove the Chairman. The President can remove the Chairman on the same grounds on which the Chairman and Members of the Union Public Service Commission can be removed. It is noteworthy that Part XIV of the Constitution of India (Articles 315 to 323) contains provisions regarding the State Public Service Commission, including its independence, powers, constitution, appointment of members, removal, etc.

stem: What is the respective strength of the national Assembly and the Senate in the new Parliament of South Africa?
expl: The strength of the National Assembly and the National Council of Provinces in the new Parliament of South Africa is 400 : 90 respectively. It may be noted that the National Council of Provinces was earlier known as the Senate. In 1997, the National Council of Provinces was constituted in place of the Senate. Therefore, if “Senate” is taken to mean the National Council of Provinces, the correct answer will be option (d).

stem: Which country in the world has declared itself a “Hindu” nation?

stem: In the United nations Security Council, which of the following countries is not a permanent member?
expl: The United Nations Security Council has five permanent members—United States of America, Britain (U.K.), France, Russia, and China. In the 15-member Security Council, the remaining 10 countries are non-permanent members elected for two years. For the 2026–27 term, Bahrain, Colombia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Latvia, and Liberia have been elected as non-permanent members of the United Nations Security Council.
